before: Sport and recreation are promoted as public health goods, and injury is the principal cost attached to them. Most injury surveillance is organised around one sport, one age group or one clinical setting, which makes the shape of the problem across the whole lifespan hard to see: a paediatric playground series and an adult overuse series cannot be laid side by side. The National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) is one of the few sources that samples every age from the same frame, with the same coding, over decades.
after: Sport and recreation are promoted as public health goods, and injuries can accompany participation. Most injury surveillance is organised around one sport, one age group or one clinical setting, which makes the shape of the problem across the whole lifespan hard to see: a paediatric playground series and an adult overuse series cannot be laid side by side. The National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) is one of the few sources that samples every age from the same frame, with the same coding, over decades.

before: Sixteen raw rows have invalid design fields. The affected-row masks for Stratum, PSU and Weight coincide; this supports a shared defect but does not prove its mechanism. Four eligible rows are excluded. No numeric zero weights were found in these files.
after: Sixteen short input fragments are rejected and logged before analysis. Seventy-eight otherwise eligible records have unknown age and are excluded from this age-focused cohort. No numeric zero weights occur among structurally valid rows.

before: NEISS encodes ages under two as 200 plus months, so 201–223 mean 1–23 months and casting Age directly creates a phantom cohort of 200-year-olds at the far right of every age axis. The raw value is preserved and the decoded value added separately. This matters more here than usual, because infants are a real part of a recreation cohort.
after: NEISS codes 201–223 as 1–23 months; 201 also covers newborns. Code 0 means unknown age, not infancy (CPSC, 2025, p. 10). The initial loader wrongly retained 78 such records, including 27 Core. The corrected loader preserves raw and decoded ages and accepts documented age codes only.

before: Eligibility is Product_1 or Product_2; Product_3 is excluded because it is empty before 2019 and would give later years more chances to qualify. Activity attribution takes the first product qualifying for the relevant cohort, otherwise Product_2. An excluded first product cannot override a qualifying second product. One row is one presentation: unique case numbers equal cohort rows in every year, verified rather than assumed, so no deduplication is required. The result is 659,664 Core and 978,925 Extended presentations.

before: Figure 1 establishes annual volume and marks the 2024 sample change. The 2020 decline is retained and tested by exclusion; the chart alone does not identify its causes. Average annual estimates are 2,334,800 Core and 3,401,000 Extended presentations. Comparisons across 2024 remain unharmonised (CPSC, 2026).
after: Figure 1 establishes annual volume and marks the 2024 sample change. The 2020 decline is retained and tested by exclusion; the chart alone does not identify its causes. before: The 2024 sample change affects comparisons across years (CPSC, 2026). A common multiplier cancels out of a proportion, but a change in relative weights between hospitals does not, so this had to be measured rather than waved away. Weighted versus unweighted comparisons describe different compositions; they do not isolate the causal effect of reweighting. Excluding 2024–2025 changes passing diagnosis cells by at most 1.76 percentage points, compared with 17.80 for Extended versus Core.

before: A second heatmap could also support comparison, but trajectories emphasise changes across ordered age groups (Heer, Bostock and Ogievetsky, 2010). Figure 4 uses trajectories instead, because the question is about shape and crossing points. Five families are drawn and the rest pooled, since eight or more lines on one axis is a legend-reading exercise; a labelled legend identifies the lines and the remainder is dashed. Colour-only distinctions among the other lines remain an accessibility limitation.

before: The result is narrower than it first looks, and the figure is built to say so. Ten activities pass every marginal-feature screen; five are excluded. Ward and average linkage use the same Euclidean representation, with 77.8% pairwise agreement, so the four-group partition is linkage-sensitive (SciPy, 2026). Full-window and through-2023 partitions agree on the nine common passing activities. This conditional stability does not validate a universal activity taxonomy. The merge heights show dissimilarity, not stability or confidence.
